messages:
alex_support: FYI — Customer AcmeRetail (high tier) opened an escalation: their hosted API is returning 5xx/gateway timeouts across many requests since ~2025-02-14T12:10:00Z. They see 502/504 and occasional 500s. They pasted a couple of request ids: req_3f9a2b, req_3f9a8d. They included a sample cURL that reliably reproduces a 502 for them.

maria_sre: Can you drop the raw server-side log snippet + headers (x-request-id, x-routing-id, trace id) and the customer's cURL? Also, do we have any global control-plane alerts?

alex_support: Pasting excerpts from their log bundle and our gateway logs (sanitized):

```
2025-02-14T12:09:59.342Z gateway INFO incoming req id=req_3f9a2b route=/v1/generate src_ip=198.51.100.23
2025-02-14T12:10:00.128Z auth-service ERROR session lookup failed user=acct:acmeretail error=500 duration=22ms trace=tr_27b
2025-02-14T12:10:00.130Z routing-policy WARN failed to select backend policy err=timeout reading config-db after 2000ms trace=tr_27b
2025-02-14T12:10:00.131Z gateway ERROR upstream 502 no healthy hosts trace=tr_27b
2025-02-14T12:10:00.132Z gateway INFO returning 502 req=req_3f9a2b

---
auth-service logs: auth-service/2025-02-14.err:
[ERROR] session-store read timeout (redis) id=acct:acmeretail:session key=...
routing-policy logs: rpc timeout -> config-db read timed out after 2000ms
config-db: saw connection pool waiters spike to 100+ and then TCP timeouts to the primary.
```

alex_support: Customer cURL (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

jordan_runtime: Thanks. That log pattern looks like control-plane dependencies timing out (auth/session read -> routing-policy can't choose a backend -> gateway returns 502/504). Did they have any recent config pushes or large rollout?

alex_support: They said they deployed a config change ~11:55 UTC that updated routing weightings; support logs show a config push at 2025-02-14T11:55:03Z by ops@acme.

maria_sre: Can we hit the routing-policy health endpoint from prod? If routing-policy /health returns anything but 200 it's likely the immediate cause. Also verify config-db (we use pgx) and redis latencies.

jordan_runtime: Running quick checks from my shell: 
```bash
# healthcheck
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://routing-policy.prod.internal/health || true
# result I got: 500
```

jordan_runtime: Also tried a direct read against config-db primary (psql) and saw intermittent timeouts ~1000ms for simple selects. Connection pool shows many waiters.

sam_prod: We need to consider customer communication — SLA impact? Acme is on reserved capacity w/ 99.9% latency/availability target. Do we open an incident page and send a status update?

alex_support: I already told the customer we're investigating and recommended a temporary workaround: force routing to their dedicated pool using an override header. They confirmed it worked for a small set of calls. Example we suggested: `X-Redwood-Force-Pool: acme-dedicated-1` — they reported success (200s) for that traffic.

maria_sre: Good quick mitigation. For root cause/action: I will attempt a rolling restart of the routing-policy pod set (non-disruptive routing fallback should handle in-flight), and jordan, can you look into config-db connection pool sizing and whether a recent config push caused a spike?

jordan_runtime: On it. Also toggled a temporary increased DB pool size on standby replica (quick patch) to relieve waiters. I'll coordinate with infra.

deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-2025-309 — control-plane timeouts affecting hosted inference (routing-policy / config-db). Pager dispatched to oncall.

maria_sre: After rolling restart, routing-policy /health returned 200 for me. I'm going to monitor error rate and any auth/service 500 spikes. Can we capture a histogram of `auth.session.latency` and `config-db.wait_time` over the last 30m?

alex_support: Customer verified a reduction in 5xx after we suggested the header workaround + after the restart they reported traffic normalized for their test cases. They still had some earlier failures.

jordan_runtime: Quick post-mortem notes: config DB connection pool exhausted due to a large concurrent config read fanout triggered by the routing weight change plus a bug that caused background revalidation to open new transactions instead of reusing cached reads. Patch applied to routing-policy to batch config reads and fixed pooled client behavior. Restarted routing-policy and auth-service sessions warmed up (session reads returned to ~8ms).

maria_sre: Final: root cause = config-db connection pool exhaustion (spike from config push + revalidation bug). Immediate mitigation = routing-policy rolling restart + increase temporary pool + direct routing override for affected customer. Long term: add circuit breaker on config reads, increase pool limits, and add an alert on connection pool waiters > 50.

sam_prod: I'll prepare a customer-facing summary and SLA impact note; recommend we notify Acme's engineering and ops leads and mark incident as resolved once metrics stable for 30m.

jordan_runtime: Monitoring windows look good at +20m. I'll stay on watch for 30 more minutes then close.

alex_support: Thanks team — I'll update the customer thread with the mitigation and planned follow-ups. :thumbsup:
